body:
All I knew before seeing the film on the big screen was that it was a movie about space, that it was filmed in Ukraine, and that it had been in development for 10 long years. Two of those three statements turned out to be true-the film is less about space and more about using the universe's depths as a theatrical backdrop, presenting the story of one... single person in the universe, as if in a locked room.

The film leaves no one indifferent, starting rather like a comedy but unfolding as a drama of human loneliness-not a dull and painful kind, like the fear of the loneliness of death, but a deep disappointment and the solitude of life.

The lead actor's performance is extraordinarily vibrant and far from flat. The original dialogue is full of dialectisms and swearing, allowing the audience to see a genuine human being, not just a character.

The sound design is superb and fully reveals the idea that every vinyl record is essentially a whole planet. If you enjoyed the Ukrainian songs, I highly recommend checking out the "Vusatyi Funk" (Moustached Funk) phenomenon; you'll love it.

Almost every frame is beautiful, and the special effects are of unbelievable quality considering the film's budget. One could nitpick certain sci-fi nuances, but they are not critical for a film that primarily tells a story about a human being, not about space.

I especially want to note that I liked the overall lore of the film and how it influenced the development of the events and characters-it was woven into the plot seamlessly.

From me, it's definitely the highest rating; I look forward to rewatching the film on its digital release.

This movie is just wonderful in every detail - the score, the set, the actors, the story. I enjoyed it so much, I laughed and cried - this is real cinema! The way it portrays Ukrainian culture is also on point and i love the autobiographical references from the director and the respectful references to other sci fi classics.

Nothing could have prepared me for this movie. I walked into the cinema knowing nothing about the plot, and - as usually happens with good films - the less you know, the better the experience.

All I knew was that it might be the first Ukrainian sci-fi film, and that everyone had been urging me to watch it.

At this point, I'm recommending you do the same. Don't watch any trailers, don't read the plot - just go in blind and let the film surprise you. It's a rollercoaster of emotions, complete with an unexpected twist and a breathtaking ending. Yes, the beginning might feel a bit unpromising, and some of the jokes miss the mark, but stay with it.

Because once the story kicks into gear, it becomes something truly special. The ship-building is bold, the atmosphere is immersive, and the emotional payoff is far stronger than I expected. It's the kind of film that lingers long after the credits roll - thought-provoking, stylish, and uniquely Ukrainian in the best way possible. (Another 10/10 goes to soundtrack)

If you're looking for something fresh, daring, and unforgettable, this movie is absolutely worth your time.

I watched this movie on a Toronto-Ukrainian Film Festival. I absolutely loved it!

It's funny, heartfelt, and filled with clever Easter eggs that only Ukrainians might catch.

The plot keeps you engaged - just when you think you've figured it out, it flips your expectations in a brilliant way. It's a perfect balance of laughter and emotion, with moments that truly move you.

What strikes me is the fact that it's basically a one-man play. The lead actor Volodymyr Kravchuk is both charismatic and charming. You really feel for him.

Beautifully crafted and creatively told, it's a story that stays with you long after the credits roll.

No pun intended - actually the movie references quite a few Science Fiction movies (Kubricks 2001 even musically). But that does not mean it does not stand on its own two feet. The fact this was done in Ukraine is even more mind boggling, considering the situation (let's call it what it is: occupation and war) ... the director is on this for almost a decade as he told us after the screening.

And he knew the ending from the beginning (is that another pun?) .. but needed the time to gather and get money to make this. He hinted at a new project ... which sounds amazing to say the least. But let's stick with this one just a bit more.

This is quite the tour de force the main character has to go through. And apart from a robot, he is alone most of the time ... will he be able to overcome and stay alive? If he does, for whom will that be? While this was conceited before the war started .. you can see parallels and you can feel the pressure ... sometimes even think: I feel there is a direct connection ... a message the movie is sending us ... in a few words ... like the ones he receives too.

The pacing is good and there are a few twists coming to at you ... the effects and the set design also are top notch. We did not talk budget, but I assume he did not have too much money ... and yet it looks amazing ... and the dialog ... just great! A fine line to have him interesting and flawed at the same time ... a "normal" human being ... a nobody ... and everything is on him now? Well let's see where he "leads us" ... a perfect ending (I would argue, no pun intended)
